Warsaw accuses Moscow of intentional provocation, but the bar for triggering NATO’s collective defence clause remains high.
Security cameras captured the moment a suspected Russian missile struck Polish territory during an attack on Ukraine on Friday. Poland’s government says it may have been hit by two missiles and a jet-powered drone.
The incident, which took place as European troops held military drills in the country and as the United States pushes to revive talks on ending the war in Ukraine, have raised questions about whether the strike was deliberate.
So what happened, and does this mean Russia has struck Poland, a NATO member?
Poland’s Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz told a news conference in Warsaw that two missiles and a jet-powered drone fell on Polish territory during Russia’s overnight attack on November 20. The missiles came down at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem, while the jet-powered drone fell at Molodycz, all in the country’s southeast.
One missile is believed to have crashed about 35km (22 miles) from where European troops’ military exercises were taking place. A Kh-101 cruise missile went down about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border, and what officials believe was a jet-powered drone hit about 30km (20 miles) from the border. No immediate injuries or damage were reported.
That night, Russia launched one of its heaviest bombardments of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia fired more than 400 drones and at least 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, some with cluster warheads. At least eight civilians were killed and more than two dozen were wounded.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it appeared “we are dealing with an intentional provocation” by Russia. He said the incident was likely timed to coincide with the European military exercises in Poland. The unprecedented two-week exercise began on November 9 in southeastern Poland and is preparing forces for a possible post-war mission in Ukraine to help stabilise the country and rebuild its military.
Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at the Clinton Institute, University College Dublin, told Al Jazeera that the incident “fits into a pattern going back for months” of Russia “testing how far they can go”.
“A few months ago, it was flying the drones into airspace , and indeed a couple of times they flew fighter jets across the border into the Baltic states,” he said. “You just test how NATO responds.”
This time, he said, Moscow had “gone a bit further”. “You lob a couple of missiles across and a drone” near where 11 countries are holding exercises.
The Polish Air Force had launched preventive air patrols on September 17 aimed at securing the eastern part of Polish airspace following repeated incursions in the previous weeks.
Harry Nedelcu, partner and senior director for geopolitics at Rasmussen Global, said the testing has not been limited to Poland.
“During the war, there’s been repeated instances of Russia testing NATO allies – Poland, Romania and also non-NATO Moldova as well, which is experiencing – especially over the last few months – increasing numbers of drones and missiles flying over its territory and airspace,” he told Al Jazeera.
He linked the incursions to one of Moscow’s core war aims. “One of the key goals in Ukraine that Russia has had in the full-scale invasion, that has lasted almost five years now, has been to prevent Ukraine from being a part of NATO,” he said. “So their goal clearly is to undermine NATO, to do everything possible to undermine it.
“What Russia is doing with these missiles, drones, that sometimes find their way into NATO territory, tests NATO just under the radar of Article 5 to see how far can they push things. How far can they take hybrid warfare?”
Under Article 5 , each member of the NATO alliance understands that if one of them is the “victim of an armed attack, each and every other member of the alliance will consider this act of violence as an armed attack against all members”.
At a meeting on Thursday with European leaders in Germany’s capital, Berlin, US President Donald Trump’s envoy and son-in-law Jared Kushner said he believes Russia would be “comfortable” with NATO-like security guarantees for post-war Ukraine.
Kushner and fellow special envoy Steve Witkoff have been holding talks with Ukraine and Russia in recent days, in a push for peace which has been viewed as sidelining Ukraine’s European allies.
Following the Berlin meeting, French President Emmanuel Macron said Ukraine’s membership of NATO should be considered again, prompting Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov to push back.
Ryabkov said any form of “quasi membership” for Kyiv of the Western ‌military alliance was totally unacceptable for Moscow, Russian state media reported.
Lucas said the timing of the missile incursion into Polish territory now is very likely tied to the ongoing US-led peace talks.
“The Russians cannot be seen to go through talks and completely exclude Europe,” he said. He described the Kremlin’s push for a “Europe-wide security architecture” as a way to avoid discussing a ceasefire or security guarantees for Ukraine.
“Rather than having a strong Europe at the talks, they want to try to divide Europe, they want to try to unsettle Europe, they want to try to scare Europe,” he said.
He also pointed to Ukraine’s recent strikes on the Kerch Bridge , which links occupied Crimea to Russia. He said these were seen as “a very serious attack on Russian capabilities” with “severe political, military and economic consequences”.
The latest Russian bombardment follows President Vladimir Putin’s pledge to retaliate against those strikes.
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called the missile incident a “grave violation” of Poland’s airspace. On X, he said the incident was “clearly dangerous” and a consequence of Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine. Rutte is expected to visit Poland this weekend.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham called it “utterly unacceptable”. Germany’s Foreign Ministry called it “yet another example of Russia’s ongoing provocations”.
US President Donald Trump had played down earlier incursions hours before. “Putin has been landing drones in Poland and a couple of little missiles, by mistake,” he said.
Nedelcu said Warsaw’s reaction was “definitely a strong one”, with Polish officials “drawing a parallel between the fact that actually around the same time there were exercises by the Coalition of the Willing [those countries willing to provide support to Ukraine] nearby, and that this may have not been a coincidence”.
He said Poland is now “asking for more NATO support under this Eastern Sentry mission that already exists”.
“It’s not if, but what form that additional support will take – maybe an airborne early warning aircraft, or something of the sort,” he said.
“But what they have stopped short of is invoking Article 4,” he added, referring to the clause under which allies consult each other before invoking Article 5. “It’s unclear whether this was at their own volition. Maybe perhaps allies don’t want to use it too often, because Article 4 is also quite serious. It has been invoked not often, and it loses its value if it’s constantly invoked.”
Lucas said the public condemnation from European leaders was itself the message to Moscow. “It’s a signal to the Russians: look, we know what you’re doing, we see what you’re doing here,” he said.
“But you’re not going to run it up into an all-out military confrontation over a couple of missiles.”
He said he expects the response to be “defensive”, built on “preparedness” of ground forces, air, naval and cyber-defence, and defence against disinformation. “These will be the most intense preparations you will have had, certainly since the 1980s and possibly well before that,” he said.

At least 11 people have died after drinking what authorities suspect was spurious alcohol in northeast India’s Manipur state, prompting an investigation.
More than 180 people, who were believed to have consumed toxic liquor, had been admitted to hospitals in Manipur as of Friday.
According to local media, officials have advised locals who have drunk alcohol from Sugnu town in Manipur in the past week to seek medical evaluation. Meanwhile, the deputy police commissioner has advised people not to drink alcohol of unknown origin.
“Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday.
Illicit alcohol is a lucrative industry in India, attracting customers who are too poor to afford licensed brands. Vendors regularly use chemicals to increase the potency of their alcohol.
Methanol is one of the substances used and can be fatal in doses as low as 60ml. Battery acid has also been found in unregulated alcohol in India.
At least 120 people died in Punjab in 2020 after drinking toxic alcohol.

PET said the individuals who allegedly tried to assassinate him were associated with a banned Danish gang named Loyal to Familia. The group is "known for extensive, serious and violent criminal activity", according to the agency.

Members of the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons fail to agree on swift adoption of legally binding rules.
The 128 countries at a United Nations conference in the Swiss city of Geneva have agreed to “elaborate” on a possible accord regulating lethal autonomous weapons, known as “killer robots”, in the next two years.
Saturday’s announcement at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) came after nearly 100 nations pushed for swift adoption of legally binding rules on the weapons capable of killing without a human making the final decision to fire.
Key arms-producing nations, including the United States, Russia and Israel, opposed the push. Decisions under the convention require the agreement of all member states.
Diplomats said Russia’s objections over procedure led to some formal sessions being called off. Talks over the final wording then ran through the night.
Julien Thoeni, the Swiss diplomat who chaired the conference, said some countries had rejected the word “negotiate”. The agreed text refers instead to the “elaboration” of an instrument.
He said more than 10 years of talks had produced a significant step for humanitarian disarmament.
“It shows that even in today’s deeply divided world, multilateral diplomacy can still deliver concrete results,” he told reporters as the meeting wrapped up.
He said the process should determine which weapons can be banned under international humanitarian law and which can be permitted but regulated.
Stop Killer Robots, a coalition of 300 organisations opposed to the development and use of autonomous weapons, called the mandate “watered down”, saying it offered no clear route to legally binding rules.
Its executive director, Nicole van Rooijen, said autonomous weapons were being deployed in combat, including systems that use artificial intelligence to choose targets.
“Delaying the creation of a legally binding instrument puts civilians and humanity at risk,” she told the AFP news agency.
Verity Coyle, deputy director for arms at Human Rights Watch, said the outcome was disappointing.
“It does not provide the urgent action needed to agree new rules – but the technology is racing ahead,” she told AFP.

An Anthropic employee and mathematician claims to have used the company's artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot to prove the famed Riemann hypothesis.
Levent Alpöge said , external on Friday, a day after Anthropic made its US stock market debut , that over the course of about six weeks, he used the Claude chatbot to create a detailed proof of the maths problem.
If found to be correct, the proof would be among the most significant in history. Alpöge described it as "one dawn across science of something far greater".
The claim comes as AI firms like OpenAI have in recent months announced scores of solutions to major higher maths problems that have eluded scholars for decades.
As for the Riemann hypothesis proof put forward on Friday, it was found using a non-public version of Anthropic's Claude.
It is a nearly 170-year-old maths problem that deals with prime numbers and is widely considered to be the single most famous problem in maths, in large part due to how complex it is.
Named after the mathematician Bernhard Riemann, the hypothesis puts forward that prime numbers have a determined order along the number line.
Prime numbers are the bedrock of higher maths, leaving breakthroughs related to them to have broad impact.
Alpöge said that he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday, asking him directly about how he could announce the discovery.
"The precise timing is horrible," Alpöge said, referring to Anthropic's public stock listing. "If I could have, I'd have finished this all much earlier."
"I am clearly unilaterally responsible for feeling I just could not live if I waited even longer. There is an obvious cynical view, to do with the timing, but it is false," he added.
The complete textual proof that Alpöge put forward in Lean, a computer language used for confirming maths proofs, is over 250,000 pages long.
Terrance Tao, a prominent mathematician, said on Friday , external that verification of the proof is still some way off.
"I imagine the digestion process will take some time, though in this case at least we have a human author to communicate with to assist with this task," Tao said.
No such human was obviously a part of major maths proofs made earlier this year using AI.
OpenAI in September claimed that employees using a non-public version of its AI tools were able to solve part of a notoriously difficult problem in just 88 hours. The problem was part of the Navier-Stokes equations, which concern how fluids move.
More than 10,000 AI agents, or computer programmed bots that operate somewhat autonomously, were put to the task as an AI training exercise.
The proof that OpenAI released on Navier-Stokes has yet to be confirmed as accurate, and it set off criticism within academic and higher maths communities and organisations about the use of AI to solve maths problems.
Anthropic has also claimed to have made other progress and solutions in maths , external and physics , external .
A group of maths scholars said , external AI companies boasting of major solutions to show how sophisticated their commercial products had become was "detrimental to the science of mathematics".
"We are witnessing a general threat to intellectual work, with misalignment between the outcome of the use of AI and its initial purpose," the scholars said in a group letter.
A month later, OpenAI released , external what it claimed were solutions, proofs, or major progress on 372 more outstanding higher maths problems.
It will take months, if not longer, for those claims to be reviewed by experts to prove their validity.

A 30-year-old man has been convicted of causing one of the most destructive wildfires in the history of Los Angeles. The verdict came after the case was retried.
A US -French man has been convicted on federal arson charges connected with the 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles, California, which killed 12 people and devastated the seaside enclave of Pacific Palisades.
The weeks-long blaze destroyed some 6,800 homes and other structures, causing estimated property losses of $150 billion (€136.7 billion).
A US District Court jury in Los Angeles found the man guilty of starting a hilltop brush fire on January 1, 2025.
While the fire was initially suppressed, it continued smoldering underground and reignited days later amid fierce winds to become the highly destructive Palisades Fire.
The man is set to be sentenced on March 17. First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli told reporters that he could face up to 40 years in prison.
The man was arrested in October 2025 , and already faced one trial five months ago that ended with a hung jury. The judge declared a mistrial in June, prompting federal prosecutors to retry the case under modified charges.
Prosecutors said security camera footage and location data from the defendant's cellphone showed he was the only person nearby when ​the January 1 blaze began in the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area.
At both trials, they characterized the man, a former Uber driver, as a loner who held a deep resentment against society, and particularly the wealthy.
The defense argued that the initial blaze could have been caused by fireworks, while prosecutors said there was no evidence that any had been set off in the area.
In March, the man denied in a court declaration that he had willfully started any fire, though he declined to testify in ⁠his own defense at either trial.
The Palisades blaze erupted almost at the same time as another wildfire that broke out in Eaton Canyon , some 30 miles (48 km) to the east.
That fire, believed to have been ignited by sparks from an electrical transmission tower, killed 19 people and devastated the Los Angeles suburb of Altadena.
Together, the two blazes rank as the deadliest wildfire disaster ever seen in Los Angeles County.

Panama's Environment Minister is pushing for language on fossil fuels to be in the final agreement
Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock, having run through the night, as countries remain unable to agree on a new global climate deal.
In a late intervention on Friday, a group of countries led by France and Panama pushed back against the draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels.
Separately, the Africa Group are fighting to get commitments on more money for adaptation, saying they did not come to the COP "to beg".
A new and potentially final agreement is expected to be published on Saturday.
More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged
Ministers from island states, Panama, and a strong contingent of EU nations which include Spain, France, Belgium, Sweden and Finland have said they are pushing to get a commitment to move away from oil, gas and coal back into the final agreement after fossil fuel producers led by Saudi pushed for its removal.
"It is not acceptable to have a COP or a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels and we simply will not put up with it," said Juan Carlos Navarro, Panama's minister for the environment.
His words were echoed by France's Minister of Ecological Transition Monique Barbut.
She took aim at several references in the text to carbon capture, use and storage - the technology that takes emissions when they are released and stores them underground - as a licence for other countries to keep burning oil and gas.
"We cannot be announcing to the world that we are now getting to 1.5 increase in the temperature and do business like nothing was happening," said France's Minister of Ecological Transition Monique Barbut.
For the first time at a COP the agreement - known officially as the Antalya Accords - acknowledges that the goal of keeping global temperature rise below 1.5C has been missed.
Beyond this point scientists warn , external that millions more people will be exposed to sea level rise and extreme heat.
The BBC understands that a number of other EU nations were asked to join the rebellion but declined, considering it unhelpful to negotiations.
Although one lead negotiator said he sympathised: "How can you have a climate agreement with no mention of the cause."
But Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister who is leading negotiations, pushed back.
He argued that this summit was about implementation, and should focus on the move towards clean energy sources.
Away from COP, renewable energy is growing at unprecedented rates. For the first time this year a modern renewable source - solar panels - contributed the largest share of global energy demand growth, outstripping oil and gas , external .
The International Energy Agency also warned this week that the longer disruption to fuel supplies through the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran War, the stronger the incentive to switch to electricity powered by renewables.
Although this week US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed at a meeting in Shenzhen to increase oil production in the face of fuel supply disruption.
It is understood that one proposal is to keep fossil fuels off the table in exchange for Saudi Arabia and other petro-states signing up to a pledge for 35% of their energy consumption to come from electricity by 2035.
This does not solve one of the other key issues raised by developing nations - the lack of money.
Earlier versions of the text included an agreement to ramp up money for adaptation to $120bn by 2035 - that has now been removed.
"We did not come here to beg we came here to claim what is rightfully ours for our people who are suffering the brunt of anthropogenic activities of developed countries," said Zanetor Agyeman Rawlings, Ghana's Environment Minister and chair of the African Group of negotiators.
Climate activists and environmental groups, who are observers to these talks, have slammed negotiations.
"I can tell you without any doubt that this has been the worst COP ever," said Mohamed Adow of Powershift Africa.
These groups are normally highly critical of the process for not moving fast enough. But it seems that Turkey have been particularly unpopular as hosts after their lead negotiator walked out of some crucial negotiations leaving many countries feeling "disrespected" said one observer.

The proposed breakthrough could reshape mathematical research, but still needs independent verification. It's the latest in a string of cases where AI has outpaced humans in solving famous maths problems.
A mathematician working for AI giant Anthropic says he used the company's Claude AI tool to solve one of mathematics most famous problems.
The Riemann hypothesis dates back to 1859 and centers on the distribution of prime numbers underpinning a much wider scope of mathematical work.
Levent Alpoge, a member of Anthropic's technical staff, made the announcement on his website. "I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis," Levent Alpoge wrote in a note released Friday .
The proof still has to be verified and confirmed by other mathematicians. If it withstands independent examination, it would be a major milestone both in mathematics and the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in scientific research.
The Riemann hypothesis is the latest and most important in a string of famous mathematical problems that were tackled with the help of AI.
Alpoge said that the collaboration with AI had generated more than 250,000 pages of mathematical material, adding that he had not yet mastered all the mathematics involved.
"Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line," he wrote. "No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line."
The Riemann Hypothesis is one of seven major mathematical problems, the so-called Millennium Prize Problems , selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which offers $1 million for a solution to each of those.
"This is an announcement of historic significance," Martin Bridson, president of the institute, said in a statement quoted by news agency AP.
He added it "holds the promise of a dramatic transformation in the perception of what is possible in the struggle to extend the human understanding of mathematics."
"But the journey from today’s announcement to a place of real understanding will be long and difficult."
Formulated by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in the 19th century, the hypothesis is about the distribution of prime numbers, which are numbers that can only be divided by themselves and the number 1.
The hypothesis describes a fundamental pattern of how these numbers are distributed as they become ever larger. Confirming that hypothesis is thought to have crucial implications for a wide range of further mathematical research.
The potential breakthrough by Alpoge and Claude AI comes amid a growing number of examples where artificial intelligence systems are making significant contributions to advanced mathematical research.
In September, rival AI company OpenAI said its technology had helped solve a problem involving the Navier-Stokes equations.
The equations, which describe the movement of fluids such as water and air, are another of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, but the claim that they've been solved also still needs independent verification.

Bayern Munich have confirmed Harry Kane will be “out for the next few months” with ankle ligament damage sustained in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday.
Kane was substituted after 20 minutes of the Bundesliga game, having been left limping after a challenge from the Cologne defender Joël Schmied. The Ballon d’Or winner was substituted and the returning Bayern coach, Vincent Kompany, said that the injury would take “months” rather than weeks to heal.
A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”
The Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore fired the visitors ahead before Kane’s injury, but Bayern levelled when Nathaniel Brown scored before the break. Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury for the second half, and Said El Mala missed an excellent late chance to earn Cologne’s first win at Bayern since 2009.
The 33-year-old may face a race to be fit for the Nations League quarter-finals, the first leg of which takes place in Norway on 27 March – just over four months away. The Bayern sporting director, Max Eberl, said on Friday that club doctors were “discussing whether or not to recommend surgery” for Kane’s injury.
Part of Kane’s recovery period will come during the Bundesliga’s winter break from 20 December to 8 January. He will, however, miss Champions League games away to Lille next week and at home to Slavia Prague next month, as well as the January trip to Manchester United and the league phase finale at home to Real Betis.
Kane’s setback adds to an extensive Bayern injury list, with Olise also going off during Friday’s game with a foot contusion. Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and Manuel Neuer were already unavailable, leaving Kompany short of options for a busy month of fixtures.
Kompany returned from his own month-long absence for Friday’s game with his arm in a sling, having dislocated his shoulder when he collapsed on a training pitch in October. The Belgian was taken to hospital for meningeal irritation treatment after his collapse, and has been recovering at home.
“I think this result was fair and Cologne deserved the point,” Kompany said after the game. “We have other worries now, I have to honestly say. We will all try together to make something strong out of this situation. FC Bayern does that time and again, and that’s what we want to do now too.”
Cologne took a surprise lead with 12 minutes gone when Moore started and finished an excellent break. The teenage winger pounced on a mislaid Olise pass and drove forward, finding Linton Maina who laid off for El Mala, whose no-look backheel pass allowed Moore to round keeper Jonas Urbig before sliding the ball home.
Kane was then brought down in the Cologne box from behind by Schmied, who got the ball first but clattered into Kane’s left leg in his follow-through. Kane’s penalty appeals were waved away, but he was left visibly limping and received treatment on his ankle before being replaced by Tom Bischof on the 20-minute mark.
The hosts levelled 17 minutes later when full-back Brown sliced a low shot into the bottom-right corner, but suffered another blow just before the break when Olise went down. The France star did not return for the second half and was seen leaving the stadium shortly after on crutches – but it appears unlikely he will miss a significant amount of time.
Just before the hour mark, El Mala and Maina forced a spectacular double save from Urbig. El Mala, recently called up by Germany, then had a golden chance to put Cologne in front with eight minutes to go when one-on-one with Urbig – but he cut his close-range shot inches wide of the post.
Now a point behind Bayern, Borussia Dortmund can move into outright first place if they win at bottom club Mönchengladbach on Saturday. Freiburg can also move level on points with Bayern if they can defeat promoted Elversberg.
This month Kane signed a new deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029, which is reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 a week, making him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses.
Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has scored an incredible 156 goals in 163 appearances, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season.

Ballon d’Or winner tears a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne.
England football captain Harry Kane will miss the “next few months” after tearing a ligament in his left ankle during Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw against Cologne on Friday.
Kane was taken down in the area by Cologne defender Joel Schmied, who reached Michael Olise’s low cross first but knocked into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg in his follow-through at the back post.
Kane writhed in pain. Although he gingerly got back to his feet and initially continued playing, he soon hobbled off the field with two physiotherapists after treatment.
A club statement on X said: “Harry Kane suffered a tear of the syndesmosis ligament in his left ankle in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga home match against Köln on Friday evening. This was confirmed by an examination by Bayern Munich’s medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be out for the next few months.”
Kane is the undisputed star of Bayern. Since joining from Spurs in 2023, he has scored 156 goals in 161 competitive fixtures and won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup.
He became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in 25 years last month and, two weeks ago, signed a new contract with Bayern that will keep him in Bavaria until June 2029.
The night was supposed to be a happy one for Bayern, who welcomed coach Vincent Kompany back to the dugout a month after he collapsed while watching the reserve squad train.
However, Kompany saw his team go behind after just 11 minutes when winger Mikey Moore, on loan from Tottenham, started and finished a counterattack.
Just nine minutes later, Kane limped off to be replaced by Tom Bischof, and the German midfielder made a quick impact. Before halftime, he found Nathaniel Brown, who fired a fierce shot into the bottom corner from the edge of the box.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has said Vladimir Putin is a "killer" in response to Donald Trump referring to the Russian leader as his "friend" in China this week.
Speaking to CNN, Zelensky said it was up to the US president "how to call Putin" but "for us, he is an enemy... for us, he's a killer".
Before Thursday's historic trilateral meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Putin, Trump called Putin his "friend" and said the two leaders have had a "great relationship for many years".
Russian attacks continued overnight, with two people killed, including a boy, and 52 injured in missile and drone strikes on Zelensky's hometown of Kryvyi Rih in the central Dnipropetrovsk region, officials said.
Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS said 11 people were also injured in the north-eastern Kharkiv region, and one person in Rivne, in the north-west.
On Friday, at least nine people were killed in Russian strikes targeting bridges in the capital Kyiv and railway stations in western Ukraine - with Zelensky calling the attack the "biggest this year" after an onslaught of 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic, and more than 400 drones.
The strikes came days after Ukraine had badly damaged the Crimean Bridge.
Hours after Friday's strikes on Ukraine, Trump told reporters at the White House that Putin would "love to end the war".
"They [Zelensky and Putin] both want to end it and it's a very good thing I have a relationship," he said on Friday.
Trump also doubled down on his description of the Russian leader as a friend but said he "can't speak" to whether Putin is a friend to the US.
However Zelensky said despite Trump's stance, he saw Putin as "a killer".
"I think mostly for the people in the world, he is a killer because he's killing - by the way- he's killing each day and night," he told CNN.
Zelensky also said speaking about Putin like he was a "friend" meant "he doesn't feel enough pressure".
The war of words came as neighbouring Poland said a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace in the south-east of the country early on Friday.
Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said the missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border.
This was about 100km from where European troops - from 11 of the 36 member nations of the coalition of the willing - were completing a training exercise, Polish authorities said. Another cruise missile and a jet-powered drone were suspected to have hit two other locations, they added.
On Saturday, Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski told the BBC the cruise missiles had guidance systems, so "it is very unlikely that they veered off course as a result of Ukrainian electronic warfare".
"This is a war in Europe that affects our security," he told Radio 4's Today programme, also referencing similar incidents in recent months across Europe.
Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.
Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned "grave violations of Polish airspace" and said the military alliance had scrambled its jets in response.
Russia has made no comment about the violations, which took place during Friday's massive attack on Ukraine.
Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

The announcement from Rockstar Games would mean GTA VI has already earned more than the entire box office run of the highest-grossing film of all time
Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales on its first day , publisher Rockstar Games has announced, calling it the biggest launch for any entertainment product in history.
The worldwide figure was based on company estimates through the end of the day Thursday, the day the game launched. Rockstar said also it had sold 32.5m units of the game on prerelease, setting a record across platforms.
“We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you,” Sam Houser, Rockstar’s president and founder, said in a statement.
The company said the sales set “a new record for entertainment across any medium … becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.”
The figure is nearly five times the roughly $800m that predecessor Grand Theft Auto V attracted during its first 24 hours in 2013 .
It also exceeds the entire box office run of Avengers: Endgame, which became the highest-grossing film of all time last month at about $2.9bn worldwide after a rerelease pushed it past Avatar.
The game went on sale Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, launching first in New Zealand and rolling out market by market as each reached midnight local time.
The release quickly became a global phenomenon, generating more social media posts than this year’s World Cup, according to monitoring platform Visibrain.
Critics praised the game, which has a score of 99 on review aggregator Metacritic.
Like its predecessors, “GTA VI” is an open-world action game in which players roam freely through a sprawling city, stealing cars, pulling off heists and carrying out missions for criminal gangs.
Its busy streets, neon-lit nightlife and beaches are rendered in striking detail, and non-player characters go about their lives whether or not the player is involved.
While critics have raved about the game, it has also prompted real-world warnings from authorities .
With the game’s release on Thursday, police departments across the US reminded people that the car thefts, reckless driving, violence and other criminal mayhem depicted in the blockbuster title should not be re-enacted on the country’s streets.
There is insufficient evidence supporting a scientific causal link between violent video games and violent behaviour, according to the American Psycyhological Association. Nonetheless, several police departments took to the internet with warnings – and even jokes – aimed at keeping GTA VI’s lawlessness firmly in the virtual world.
The Atlanta police department delivered one of the clearest messages in a social media post.
“GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is!” the department warned. “Don’t confuse virtual entertainment with real-life decisions.”

An armed robot developed by Turkish defense companies is demonstrated at a facility in Duzce, Turkey, on April 29. Omer Urer/Anadolu via Getty Images hide caption
Efforts to set firm rules on AI-powered killer robots and drones ran aground Saturday as U.N.-backed talks in Geneva produced a softened agreement to extend discussions for two more years.
Scores of countries ended the week-long U.N. conference on weapons by agreeing to "elaborate" a possible accord on such lethal autonomous weapons systems by 2028. But they didn't commit to binding rules sought by U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres, many countries, and activists.
The outcome underscored the difficulty of achieving concrete results in diplomacy amid global conflicts and major military powers jockeying for dominance.
Izumi Nakamitsu, the U.N. high representative for disarmament affairs, hailed a "significant achievement" but acknowledged a "glass half full or half empty" scenario, citing Guterres' hopes for a legally binding deal this year.
Activists accused military powers like Russia and the United States of blocking stronger language.
Stop Killer Robots lamented a "watered-down mandate," and Beatrice Fihn, founder of international law advocacy group Lex International, said the decision amounts to "pushing the can down the road for two more years."
They noted most countries supported work toward a new treaty, and Max Tegmark, a machine learning specialist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and founder of the Future of Life Institute, said: "States have agreed it is sufficient to just talk about the issue, for the 14th year, while these weapons enable atrocities."
Before the meeting, seven countries proposed launching negotiations on a rulebook that could prevent or limit the ability of machines to kill without human control or accountability. That effort fell short.
"Technology is moving faster than diplomacy," said Ambassador Frederico Meyer of Brazil, which joined Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Mexico, New Zealand and Panama in proposing such negotiations. "Diplomats are very slow."
After years of talks on the issue, advocacy groups bemoaned obstructionism largely by Russia, which, like other top AI weapons-developing countries such as the United States, wants a freer hand to develop such high-tech weapons.
Guterres, who leaves office at the end of the year, set a 2026 deadline for launching negotiations toward an agreement on autonomous weapons systems.
Pope Leo XIV and many advocacy and humanitarian groups have framed the issue as an existential debate, urging quick action to rein in AI weapons before they become too commonplace to regulate easily.
Activists say armed drones that can independently strike targets have already been deployed in some select instances in conflict zones, but widespread rollout hasn't happened.
Talks this week centered on the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, ratified by 128 countries, where decisions are made by consensus. That means any single country can thwart an agreement, and that any deal was likely to be based on a low common denominator.

texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9zr:
Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) saw record retail sales in its first full-day of release , hitting $3.8bn (£2.9bn), making it the biggest entertainment launch in history.
Take-Two, the parent company of Rockstar Games, said on Friday the figures were based on estimates through end of day on Thursday and marked a record for "entertainment across any medium". It pre-sold 32.5m copies of the game.
To compare, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, this year's highest-grossing film so far, made $2.5bn (£1.8bn) over its entire run in cinemas .
Internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare said earlier that PS5 downloads in the UK peaked at 8.6 times normal levels around its launch.
New Zealand, where GTA 6 was first available, saw a 14.8-fold spike four hours before, suggesting some players switched regions for early access .
In its initial findings since the game's launch, Cloudflare also recorded a huge surge in traffic to Rockstar's online services, peaking at 11.2 times normal levels in Australia and 9.3 times on the US East Coast.
In Europe, UK interest was particularly strong, reaching seven times normal levels compared with 5.3 times in France and Germany.
The record smashes that of its predecessor - from 13 years prior - Grand Theft Auto V. The game previously held the best opening week sales in video-game history, earning $1.15bn (£1.2bn) in just five days.
The game is the latest instalment in Rockstar's nearly three decade old crime simulator franchise, which has become one of the most popular games in history .
At its core, the series is a satirical take on the American dream, putting players in the shoes of career criminals in Leonida, the game's Florida-inspired state.
The latest release follows new characters, a pair of small-time criminals Lucia and her partner Jason.
GTA 6 is estimated to have cost more than $1bn to develop , which would make it the most expensive video game in history.
BBC News Mundo’s Rafael Rojas visits the real-life Miami locations that inspired GTA 6's Vice City.
Research firm Sensor Tower said GTA 6 will be so popular that it will reduce the time gamers spend on other single-player titles by 10%.
The firm said its estimates are based on email receipts data and other statistical sources that track millions of people daily. They also track public profiles across major gaming platforms like PlayStation and Xbox, where GTA 6 is available.
Around three quarters of the game's sales have been on PlayStation 5 and the balance on Xbox, Sensor Tower said.
Niko Partners, a gaming market research firm, said it expects GTA 6 to make more than $3bn in sales worldwide this year.
That figure would rank GTA 6 among the highest-grossing entertainment releases ever, but it would still have some way to go to catch 1939's Gone with the Wind , which has made an estimated $4.5bn (£3.44bn), adjusted for inflation.
Rockstar is expected to make even more money from GTA 6 over the coming years.
The New York-based studio has yet to announce when the game will be released for PCs or given a date for its multiplayer expansion, which will allow players to interact and go on missions with others over the internet.
If 2013's GTA 5 is any guide, multiplayer will add dozens more hours of gameplay and bring in even more revenue for Rockstar as players spend real money on in-game property, cars and other perks.
Anticipation for the blockbuster title has grown through repeated delays, following a 13-year wait.
GTA 6 has been hailed by some reviewers as one of the most impressive gaming experiences ever. Entertainment media site IGN described it as an "uncompromisingly engineered" masterpiece.
The release of GTA 6 at midnight on Thursday across various time zones saw many gamers stay up through the night, while some took the following day off to play.
The launch broke Virgin Media O2's evening traffic record as people rushed to install GTA 6's huge 212GB file on consoles.
The game's graphic content has resulted in censorship in Japan and, like earlier GTA releases, is not approved for sale in mainland China.
Police departments have also reminded Americans that street racing, auto theft and gun violence are still crimes in real life, as excitement reached a fever pitch in the US.

All options open in future talks, says Ed Miliband, while prime minister hails ‘a good day for Britain and Europe’
The UK rejoining the EU could be on the table in informal discussions between Andy Burnham and European leaders in Brussels, Ed Miliband has said.
The foreign secretary said “all options” would be examined in the process, after the prime minister agreed deals on trade and young people with the bloc on Friday.
Agreements on food and drink standards, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme were announced after talks this week. Under the plans, 100,000 young Britons will be allowed to live, work, study and travel in the EU, with similar access for Europeans in the UK.
Burnham said the agreement would add 0.5% to the UK’s GDP, a £17bn boost to the British economy.
Miliband said Burnham would have further “brainstorming” discussions with the EU in the next year about what could happen next. He said the agreements this week were the limit of what could be done before the next general election.
However, the trio of deals could be derailed in six months, as the EU threatened to block them unless the UK allows European students to pay domestic-level fees to study at British universities.
Miliband said in an interview for the BBC’s Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that “all the options will be on the table” when pressed on whether rejoining the bloc would be considered, adding: “We will look at the benefits and the costs of all the different options.”
Since entering government in 2024, Labour has stuck to the “red lines” in its manifesto, which stated the party would not rejoin the single market or customs union. It also ruled out freedom of movement.
Burnham has previously said he wants to see the UK rejoin the EU in his lifetime.
The prime minister will use the announcement of his 10-year plan before Christmas to explore how the UK could get closer to the EU after the next election. Informal discussions will take place with Brussels before next year’s UK-EU summit.
Miliband said he accepts the result of the 2016 vote but “the world has changed massively”.
“Europe is changing too, so we’ve got to look at what that means,” he said. “It’s not about this parliament, we’re respecting the red lines in this parliament.”
He also denied the deal with the EU would rely on progress in discussions on students from the bloc coming to the UK. It has been reported that a proposal from the bloc to lower the level of tuition fees paid by EU students in the UK has not been agreed.
Miliband told the BBC it was “absolutely clear” the agreements on food exports, energy and youth mobility would apply, even though there has not been a deal on tuition fees.
The foreign secretary said: “The dates are set out in 2028 when these things are coming in, we’re introducing legislation in parliament, so definitely.”
On Friday, Burnham said the agreement represented a “good day for Britain and Europe”. He said the agreements answer “the biggest challenges of our times and the biggest worries that people have”, citing the cost of living, lack of economic growth, illegal immigration and challenges facing young people.
“The deal is done. It is there in black and white in front of you,” Burnham said, adding that the legislation would enter parliament next week.
The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, played down the disagreement, saying she was “confident we are going to find a solution”. About the further discussions, she said: “We welcome this brainstorming, so count on us.”
The environment secretary, Angela Eagle, told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Saturday the deal was good for farmers. “(It) will open up new markets. They’ll be able to import and expor. This is a win-win for the UK. We will dissolve a lot of the friction and costs at the border for UK agriculture and food.”

Altın piyasasında hafta sert bir düşüşle kapandı. Cuma günü yüzde 3,48 değer kaybeden gram altın 5.731,95 liraya inerek 6 bin liranın altında kaldı. Ons altın ise 3.525 dolar civarında, Eylül 2025'ten bu yana en düşük seviyelerde bulunuyor. Piyasalar hafta sonu kapalı olduğu için Cumartesi günü cuma kapanış fiyatları geçerli. Gram altın ne kadar? Çeyrek altın ne kadar? İşte 21 Kasım güncel altın fiyatları.
Düşüşün arkasında iki ana etken var: Fed'in faiz artırımı beklentisi ve güçlenen dolar . Piyasa fiyatlamalarına göre Fed'in Aralık toplantısında faizi 25 baz puan artırma olasılığı yüzde 94'e çıktı. Fed'in son toplantısına ait tutanaklarda da karar alıcıların neredeyse tamamının faizlerin daha yukarı taşınması gerekebileceği görüşünü paylaştığı aktarıldı.
Dolar endeksi bu hafta Nisan 2025'ten bu yana en yüksek noktasına çıktı. Faiz getirisi olmayan altını elde tutmanın maliyeti artarken, dolar cinsinden fiyatlanan metal diğer para birimleriyle alım yapanlar için pahalılaştı. ABD borsalarında yapay zekâ şirketlerinin hisselerindeki gerileme de piyasalardaki dalgalanmayı artırdı.
Haftalık bazda ons altındaki kaybın yüzde 9'a yaklaştığı belirtiliyor. Bazı değerlendirmelerde gram altının uzun süredir devam eden yükseliş eğiliminin de baskı altında olduğu, bu serinin sürüp sürmediğinin dönem kapanış verileriyle netleşeceği ifade ediliyor.
Küresel piyasalar hafta sonu kapalı olduğundan altında yeni fiyatlama pazartesi günü başlayacak. Yurt içinde gram ve çeyrek altın, ons altının yanı sıra dolar /TL kurunun seyrine bağlı olarak değişmeye devam edecek. Dolar/TL cumartesi sabahı 50,57 lira seviyesinde bulunuyor.
Yatırımcıların yeni haftada gözü Fed'in aralık ayındaki faiz kararına ilişkin beklentilerde, ABD 'den gelecek enflasyon ve faiz mesajlarında ve dolar endeksinin seyrinde olacak. Güçlü dolar ve yükselen faiz beklentisi sürerse altın üzerindeki satış baskısının devam edebileceği, bu verilerde yumuşama görülürse ise tepki alımlarının gündeme gelebileceği belirtiliyor.

Aile komedisi türünün bilinen yapımları arasında yer alan Evde Tek Başına (Home Alone), uzun bir aranın ardından serinin yıldızı Macaulay Culkin ile yeni bir film projesiyle gündeme geldi. Deadline'ın aktardığına göre Disney, ilk iki filmde Kevin McCallister karakterini canlandıran Culkin'in başrolde olacağı yeni film için çalışmalara başladı.
İddiaya göre 46 yaşındaki Macaulay Culkin, geçen yaz Disney Live Action ve 20th Century Studios Başkanı David Greenbaum ile bir araya gelerek yeni film fikrini paylaştı. Görüşmenin ardından başlatılan süreçte Culkin'in yalnızca başrolde yer almakla kalmayıp hikayenin geliştirilmesine de katkı sunacağı ifade edildi.
Yeni filmin senaryosunu Seth Rogen ile Evan Goldberg'in kaleme alacağı öne sürüldü. Culkin'in fikri üzerinde oyuncuyla birlikte çalışan ikilinin projede yapımcı olarak da yer alacağı kaydedildi. Konusu ve ayrıntıları henüz açıklanmayan filmin, klasik hikayeyi yetişkin bir Kevin McCallister perspektifinden ele alabileceği belirtiliyor.
1990 yapımı ilk Evde Tek Başına filmi, ailesinin Paris'e giderken evde unuttuğu Kevin McCallister'ın iki hırsıza karşı verdiği mücadeleyi anlatıyordu. Macaulay Culkin, 1992 tarihli Evde Tek Başına 2'de de aynı rolle izleyici karşısına çıkarken, serinin üçüncü ve dördüncü filmleri farklı oyuncu kadrolarıyla çekilmişti. İlk iki filmin yönetmeni Chris Columbus'un ise yeni projede yer alıp almayacağı henüz bilinmiyor.
İlk iki filmin yönetmeni Chris Columbus, yeni film duyurusunun hemen öncesinde Variety'e yaptığı değerlendirmede serinin devamına ilişkin görüşlerini paylaştı. Seride Kevin'ın annesi Kate'i canlandıran ve 30 Ocak'ta 71 yaşında yaşamını yitiren Catherine O'Hara olmadan geri dönüşün çok zor olduğunu belirten Columbus, şu ifadeleri kullandı:
"Her zaman söylediğim gibi, Catherine ‘Evde Tek Başına’nın %50’sini oluşturuyordu. Catherine O’Hara ve Macaulay Culkin filmde olmasaydı bu film de olmazdı. Çünkü filmin duygusal merkezini onlar oluşturuyor."

The Wall Street Journal'ın haberine göre, Anthropic araştırmacısı Alpöge, matematiğin çözülmemiş en meşhur problemlerinden olan Riemann hipotezinin çözümüne dair bir kanıt bulmak için yapay zekayla çalıştığını belirtti.
Yapay zeka modeli Claude'un yardımıyla bu hipotezin çözümünü bulduğuna inandığını kişisel internet sitesinde açıklayan Alpöge, söz konusu kanıtı bilgisayarların doğrulayabileceği bir programlama dilinde yayımladı.
Alpöge, konuya ilişkin "Matematiğin devrim yaşadığı bu dönemde, umarım bu argüman önümüzde bizi bekleyen mucizelere bir bakış açısı sunar ve en basit şeylerde keşfetmek üzere olduğumuz neşeyi ve hayranlığı bize gösterir." ifadesini kullandı.
Alpöge'nin çözümü doğrulanırsa, bu olay yapay zeka tarafından çözülen ikinci "Milenyum Ödülü Sorusu" olarak tarihe geçecek.
Riemann hipotezi, 1859 yılında ortaya atıldığından beri kanıtlanamadı. Asal sayıların nasıl dağıldığını öngören bu hipotez, 167 yıldır matematikçiler tarafından çözülmeyi bekliyor.
Hipotez 2000 yılında çözülmesi son derece zor olduğu bilinen yedi "Milenyum Ödülü Problemi"nden biri olarak seçilmişti.
Eğer söz konusu hipotezin çözümü teyit edilirse, insanlar 26 yılda bu problemlerden yalnızca birinin sonucuna ulaşırken, yapay zeka modelleri sadece 3 ay içerisinde bu problemlerden ikisini çözmüş olacak.
Anadolu Ajansı web sitesinde, AA Haber Akış Sistemi (HAS) üzerinden abonelere sunulan haberler, özetlenerek yayımlanmaktadır. Abonelik için lütfen iletişime geçiniz.
Bu haberde bir hata mı var? Her türlü talep, şikâyet ve görüş için okur temsilcimize ulaşabilirsiniz.

Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, 21 Kasım Cumartesi için Doğu Karadeniz'den Hatay'a uzanan geniş bir hatta 21 ile sarı kodlu uyarı verdi. Kuvvetli sağanağın yanı sıra iç ve doğu kesimlerde güney yönlü rüzgarın saatte 40-60 kilometre hızla esmesi bekleniyor. Hava sıcaklığı kuzey ve iç bölgelerde 2 ila 6 derece birden düşecek.
MeteoUyarı haritasında bugün sarıya dönen iller şöyle: Artvin , Ardahan , Bayburt , Batman , Bingöl , Diyarbakır , Erzincan , Erzurum , Giresun , Gümüşhane , Hatay , Kahramanmaraş , Muş , Ordu , Osmaniye , Rize , Samsun , Sivas , Tokat , Trabzon ve Tunceli . Listenin ağırlığı Karadeniz ile Doğu Anadolu'da toplanırken Akdeniz 'in doğusundaki üç il de uyarı kapsamına alındı.
Kurumun sabah yayımladığı bültene göre yağışların Doğu Karadeniz, Doğu Anadolu'nun kuzeyi, Hatay kıyıları, Osmaniye , Kahramanmaraş , Ordu , Tokat , Sivas , Bingöl ve Muş çevrelerinde kuvvetli olacağı tahmin ediliyor. Uyarıda ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım ve ulaşımda aksamalara karşı dikkatli olunması istendi.
Kuvvetli yağış uyarısı yalnızca sarı kodlu illerle sınırlı değil. Bartın , Karabük , Kastamonu , Sinop ve Yozgat çevreleri ile Ankara , Eskişehir ve Kırıkkale'nin kuzey ilçelerinde de yer yer kuvvetli sağanak bekleniyor.
Karadeniz'de en sert tablo Rize ve Trabzon 'da görülecek. Her iki kentte de gün boyu kuvvetli sağanak ve gök gürültülü sağanak öngörülüyor, termometreler 17 dereceyi geçmeyecek. Artvin , Giresun ve Ordu 'da aralıklı sağanak yer yer şiddetini artıracak. Samsun 'da gök gürültülü sağanak beklenirken iç kesimdeki Tokat , yağışın kuvvetli olacağı iller arasında gösterildi.
Doğu Karadeniz'in iç kesimlerinde, özellikle 2000 metrenin üzerindeki yüksek kesimlerde yağışın karla karışık yağmura, yer yer kara dönmesi bekleniyor. Gümüşhane ve Bayburt 'ta yayla yollarını kullanacak sürücülerin buzlanma ve görüş mesafesine karşı tedbirli olması gerekiyor.
Doğu Anadolu'da Erzurum için bugün çok bulutlu ve aralıklı yağmurlu bir gün öngörülüyor. Kentte yağışların akşam ve gece saatlerinde kuvvetlenmesi, yükseklerde karla karışık yağmura dönmesi bekleniyor; en yüksek sıcaklık 13 derece. Ardahan , Erzincan ve Tunceli de uyarı listesine girerken Bingöl ve Muş çevresinde yağışın kuvvetli olacağı belirtildi.
Bugünkü uyarının ikinci ayağı rüzgar. Meteoroloji'ye göre güney yönlü rüzgar Marmara'nın güneyi, İç Ege, Akdeniz 'in iç kesimleri, İç Anadolu, Orta ve Doğu Karadeniz'in iç kesimleri ile Doğu Anadolu'da kuvvetli esecek. Saatte 40-60 kilometreyi bulacak rüzgar nedeniyle çatı uçması, ağaç ve direk devrilmesi gibi olumsuzluklara karşı uyarı yapıldı. Karadeniz, Marmara ve Akdeniz'de denizlerde de fırtınamsı rüzgar bekleniyor.
Güneydoğu'da Diyarbakır 'da akşam saatlerinden sonra sağanak geçişleri görülecek; Batman de uyarı verilen iller arasında. Akdeniz'de ise Hatay kıyıları, Osmaniye ve Kahramanmaraş çevresinde öğleden sonra yağışın kuvvetlenmesi bekleniyor. Hatay 'da en yüksek sıcaklık 22 derece civarında seyredecek.
İç Anadolu'da Sivas için kuvvetli yağmur ve sağanak tahmini yapıldı, kentte hava sıcaklığı 14 dereceye kadar gerileyecek.

Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, 21 Kasım için 21 ilde sarı kodlu uyarı yayımladı. Yurdun birçok bölgesinde kuvvetli sağanak ve gök gürültülü yağış beklenirken rüzgarın hızının saatte 60 kilometreye ulaşacağı tahmin ediliyor. Hafta sonundaki yağışlı havanın ardından yeni haftada sıcaklıklar sert düşecek. İstanbul'da pazartesi günü 19 derece olması beklenen hava sıcaklığı, çarşamba günü 9 dereceye kadar gerileyecek.
Türkiye, Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğünün son tahminlerine göre yağışlı ve hareketli bir hava sisteminin etkisine giriyor. 21 Kasım Cumartesi günü birçok bölgede sağanak ve gök gürültülü sağanak yağış beklenirken, yeni haftayla birlikte sıcaklıklarda belirgin düşüş yaşanacak.
Meteoroloji'nin değerlendirmelerine göre kuzey ve iç kesimlerde hava sıcaklıkları 2 ila 6 derece azalacak. Doğu Karadeniz'in iç kesimleri ile Doğu Anadolu'nun kuzeydoğusunda yüksek kesimlerde karla karışık yağmur ve yer yer kar yağışı görülecek.
Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü, 21 Kasım Cumartesi günü beklenen kuvvetli yağış nedeniyle 21 il için sarı kodlu uyarı yayımladı.
Uyarı kapsamındaki bölgelerde kuvvetli yağış ve gök gürültülü sağanak bekleniyor. Vatandaşların ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım, heyelan ve ulaşımda yaşanabilecek aksamalara karşı dikkatli olması isteniyor.
21 Kasım tahminlerine göre yurt genelinde parçalı ve çok bulutlu bir hava etkili olacak. Marmara'nın kuzey ve doğusu, İç Ege, Doğu Akdeniz, İç Anadolu'nun kuzey ve doğusu, Karadeniz, Doğu Anadolu, Güneydoğu Anadolu'nun kuzey ve batısı ile Antalya ve Isparta çevrelerinde sağanak ve gök gürültülü sağanak yağış bekleniyor.
Doğu Karadeniz'in iç kesimleri ile Doğu Anadolu'nun kuzeydoğusunda 2 bin metre üzerindeki yüksek kesimlerde ise karla karışık yağmur ve yer yer kar yağışı görülecek.
Yağışla birlikte kuvvetli rüzgar da etkisini gösterecek. Marmara'nın güneyi, İç Ege, Akdeniz'in iç kesimleri, İç Anadolu, Orta ve Doğu Karadeniz'in iç kesimleri ile Doğu Anadolu'da rüzgarın güneyli yönlerden saatte 40 ila 60 kilometre hızla esmesi bekleniyor.
Karadeniz, Marmara ve Akdeniz açıklarında ise fırtınamsı rüzgar etkili olacak. Kuvvetli rüzgar nedeniyle yaşanabilecek olumsuzluklara karşı vatandaşların tedbirli olması gerekiyor.
Hafta sonundaki yağışların ardından 23 Kasım Pazartesi günü Marmara Bölgesi'nde gök gürültülü sağanak, Ege kıyılarında ise yağış bekleniyor. Pazartesi günü İstanbul'da sıcaklığın 19 dereceye kadar yükselmesi, gece saatlerinde ise 13 derece civarında seyretmesi öngörülüyor.
Ancak bu yükseliş uzun sürmeyecek. 24 Kasım Salı gününden itibaren soğuk hava dalgası etkisini hissettirecek. İstanbul'da sıcaklığın salı günü 10 dereceye kadar gerilemesi, gece saatlerinde ise 8 derece olması bekleniyor.
25 Kasım Çarşamba günü soğuk hava etkisini sürdürecek. İstanbul'da gündüz sıcaklığı 9 dereceye, gece sıcaklığı ise 4 dereceye kadar düşecek.
Sıcaklık düşüşü başkent Ankara'da da hissedilecek. 21 Kasım'da 14 derece olması beklenen hava sıcaklığı, 23 Kasım Pazartesi günü 16 dereceye kadar çıkacak. Salı günü 12 dereceye gerilemesi beklenen sıcaklık, çarşamba günü ise 7 dereceye kadar düşecek. Gece sıcaklığının 3 dereceye inmesi öngörülüyor.
Yeni haftayla birlikte kış şartları özellikle doğu bölgelerinde etkisini artıracak. Salı günü Ardahan, Kars, Erzurum ve Bayburt çevrelerinde kar yağışı beklenirken, çarşamba günü Gümüşhane'de de kar görülecek. Sivas ve Ağrı çevrelerinde ise karla karışık yağmur etkili olacak.
Batı bölgelerinde de gece sıcaklıkları düşecek. Edirne, Kırklareli ve Uşak'ta çarşamba gecesi sıcaklıkların sıfır dereceye kadar gerilemesi bekleniyor.
Meteoroloji'nin uyarıları doğrultusunda vatandaşların kuvvetli yağış, ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım ve kuvvetli rüzgara karşı dikkatli olması gerekiyor. Yeni haftada beklenen ani sıcaklık düşüşü nedeniyle özellikle gece ve sabah saatlerinde tedbirli olunması önem taşıyor.

27 Kasım’da vizyona girecek filmin hem başrolünü hem de ortak yapımcılığını üstlenen Hazar Ergüçlü, duygularını şu sözlerle dile getirdi: “Heyecandan karnım ağrıyor. Böyle bir filmin parçası olmak benim için çok değerli.”
Dünya prömiyerini Tribeca Film Festivali’nde, Türkiye prömiyerini ise Adana Altın Koza Film Festivali’nde gerçekleştiren “Mutter: Bir Annenin Hatıra Defteri” özel bir gösterimle izleyici karşısına çıktı. Atlas 1948 Sineması’ndaki gösterime film ekibinin yanı sıra sanat, iş ve cemiyet dünyasından çok sayıda isim katıldı.
Altın Koza’da ‘en iyi kadın oyuncu’ ödülünü kazanan Hazar Ergüçlü , heyecanını dile getirerek filmi izlemeye gelenlere teşekkür etti. Yönetmen Alphan Eşeli ise filmin kendisi için taşıdığı anlamı, “Bu film yaptığım belki de en kişisel iş. Çok özel bir proje. Zor şartlarda yaptık ama çok şanslıydım, harika bir ekiple çalıştım” sözleriyle anlattı.
Filmde Ercan karakterine hayat veren Güven Kıraç, konuşmasında “Bu filmi sinema kariyerimde oynadığım en enteresan filmlerden biri olarak nitelendiriyorum. Türkiye’de böyle bir filmin çekildiğine daha önce çok şahit olmadım” dedi.
Ulvi Kahyaoğlu da “Geldiğiniz için çok teşekkür ederiz. Umarım filmimizi herkes beğenir” sözleriyle davetlilere seslendi. 27 Kasım’da sinemalarda Annelik ve hayatta kalma içgüdüsünün sınırlarında ilerleyen sürükleyici bir hikâyeyi konu alan “ Mutter: Bir Annenin Hatıra Defteri ”, 27 Kasım’da CJ ENM dağıtımıyla gösterime girecek.
Filmin görüntü yönetmenliğini Özkan Karaköse, kurgusunu Mesut Ulutaş üstlenirken ses tasarımında Hervé Guyader ve Cenker Kökten’in, özgün müziklerinde ise Tristan Bechet’nin imzası bulunuyor.
Filmin konsept tasarımları da “Alien: Covenant” ve “Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga” gibi yapımlarda çalışan Matt Hatton tarafından hazırlandı.

Kitap dünyasına açılan kapınızı aralayın! En sevdiğiniz kitapları indirimli fiyatlarla keşfedin ve hayal gücünüzü genişletin.
Piyasalarda geride kalan haftada yatırım araçlarının performansı ayrıştı. Haftalık bazda dolar ve İsviçre frangı yatırımcısına sınırlı da olsa kazanç sağlarken; Borsa İstanbul (BIST 100) ve altın cephesinde sert değer kayıpları yaşandı. 24 ayar külçe gram altın haftayı yüzde 7,60 düşüşle kapatırken, BIST 100 endeksindeki haftalık kayıp yüzde 6’yı aştı.
Borsa İstanbul’da Sert Satış: BIST 100 Yüzde 6,01 Düştü
Borsa İstanbul'da BIST 100 endeksi, haftayı yüzde 6,01 azalışla 11.131,32 puandan tamamladı. Endeks, hafta boyunca en düşük 11.102,52 puanı, en yüksek ise 11.951,86 puanı test etti.
Sektör endekslerinin tamamında negatif bir seyir izlenirken, en sert düşüş sanayi tarafında görüldü:
BIST 100 endeksine dahil hisseler arasında haftanın en çok prim yapan hissesi yüzde 13,82 artışla Ege Gübre oldu. Onu yüzde 2,73 yükselişle Türk Hava Yolları ve yüzde 1,44 artışla Tofaş Türk Otomotiv izledi.
Haftanın en çok değer kaybeden hisseleri ise şu şekilde sıralandı:
Öte yandan Borsa İstanbul’da işlem gören şirketler arasında piyasa değeri sıralamasında zirve değişmedi. Kitap dünyasına açılan kapınızı aralayın! En sevdiğiniz kitapları indirimli fiyatlarla keşfedin ve hayal gücünüzü genişletin.
Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü (MGM) , 21 Kasım Cumartesi günü için yayımladığı hava tahmin raporunda yurdun büyük bölümünde yağış beklendiğini duyurdu. Birçok bölgede sağanak ve gök gürültülü sağanak yağışın etkili olması beklenirken yüksek kesimlerde karla karışık yağmur ve kar görülecek.
Marmara’nın kuzey ve doğusu, İç Ege, Doğu Akdeniz, İç Anadolu’nun kuzey ve doğusu, Karadeniz, Doğu Anadolu ile Güneydoğu Anadolu’nun bazı kesimlerinde yağış tahmin ediliyor. Antalya ve Isparta çevrelerinde de sağanak bekleniyor.
Meteoroloji, özellikle Doğu Karadeniz ve Doğu Anadolu’nun kuzeyinde yağışların kuvvetli olacağı uyarısında bulundu. Hatay kıyıları, Osmaniye, Kahramanmaraş, Bartın, Karabük, Kastamonu, Sinop, Ordu, Tokat, Yozgat, Sivas, Bingöl ve Muş çevreleri de kuvvetli yağış beklenen yerler arasında sıralandı.
Ankara, Eskişehir ve Kırıkkale’nin kuzey ilçelerinde de kuvvetli yağış görülebileceği belirtildi. Yetkililer; ani sel, su baskını, yıldırım ve ulaşımda yaşanabilecek aksamalara karşı yurttaşların tedbirli olmasını istedi.
Hava sıcaklıklarının kuzey ve iç kesimlerde 2 ila 6 derece düşmesi, diğer bölgelerde ise önemli bir değişiklik yaşanmaması bekleniyor. Doğu Karadeniz’in iç kesimlerindeki yüksek alanlarla Doğu Anadolu’nun kuzeydoğusunda yağışların karla karışık yağmur ve yer yer kar şeklinde görüleceği tahmin ediliyor.
Rüzgârın genel olarak güneyli yönlerden orta kuvvette eseceği, bazı bölgelerde ise hızının saatte 40 ila 60 kilometreye ulaşacağı öngörülüyor. Marmara’nın güneyi, İç Ege, Akdeniz’in iç kesimleri, İç Anadolu, Orta ve Doğu Karadeniz’in iç kesimleri ile Doğu Anadolu’da kuvvetli rüzgâr bekleniyor.
Meteoroloji, kuvvetli rüzgârın neden olabileceği olumsuzluklara karşı da dikkatli ve tedbirli olunması gerektiğini bildirdi.

No details have been announced for next year's TRNSMT festival
We're just weeks away from Christmas but for many music fans their thoughts have already turned to next summer's festival season.
Glastonbury announced its line-up this week , tickets are on sale for Reading and Leeds and the headliners for Belladrum have been announced.
But there is silence surrounding the TRNSMT plans for next year. Event promoters DF Concerts has declined to confirm whether it will return in 2027.
No dates, ticket sales or acts have yet been announced for the Glasgow Green festival, which has been running since 2017.
BBC Scotland News has spoken to several music industry professionals who have been involved with the event previously. All said they had yet to hear any details about 2027 - something described as unusual and different to past years.
It follows a 2026 edition where reduced tickets were being offered on discount websites.
The concert promoter is understood to have several dates booked in for Glasgow Green next year, but it is unknown whether these are for a festival or for one-off big shows on the green.
TRNSMT sold some tickets at half price for this year's event
Two large gigs have already been announced for the green space by rock band Fontaines D.C. and the singer Alex Warren.
Both of those gigs have been advertised by DF under branding saying Live At Glasgow Green.
Multiple sources told BBC Scotland News they would not be surprised if several large gigs replace TRNSMT going forward.
DF Concerts previously claimed TRNSMT was worth an estimated £16.6m to Glasgow.
However, it has faced criticism in recent years over lack of diversity among headliners - with no women topping the bill in the event's history - and the same acts regularly playing the festival.
BBC Scotland News has spoken to people in a number of roles across the music business, from band management to PRs and people involved with setting up stages.
All said there had been silence regarding any plans for TRNSNT, and none knew of any bands booked for it.
When asked for information about TRNSMT, DF Concerts said there was no information on the event it could share at this time.
A follow-up question that asked if the promoter could confirm if the festival was being planned for next year was given the same response.
Plenty of Saltires will be on show as Scotland's game is screened to the TRNSMT crowd
Last year the festival's dates for 2026 were announced on 3 November with the line-up revealed three days later.
Richard Ashcroft, Kasabian and Lewis Capaldi topped the bill, with the event held in June this year - a month earlier than usual .
Other acts who played included Wolf Alice, CMAT, the Fratellis and the Snuts.
Discount platform itison later offered tickets for the festival at £49 a night, considerably down from the £82 they were initially offered at - although the reduced tickets did sell out.
Music journalist Craig McConnell, deputy editor with long-running Scottish fanzine is this music? , external and a regular at TRNSMT, said he would not be surprised if the festival does not go ahead.
He believes the likes of Summer Sessions - large outdoor shows at venues like Bellahouston Park - have supplanted TRNSMT.
"Over the past few years it's been clear that big summer gigs such as the Summer Sessions attract a larger and more engaged audience than TRNSMT, regardless of respective capacity," he said.
"Where TRNSMT has appeared to try to appeal to everyone with their line-up and ended up pleasing no-one, Summer Sessions allows for a tightly curated bill of aligned artists with a much more flexible schedule. It would make business sense to make a shift."
Several music festivals in Scotland did not go ahead in 2026, repeating a wider pattern across the UK.
Over the past decade other Scottish events like the Wickerman and Connect - another DF event - have also gone .
Rebecca Wallace, a lecturer in commercial music at the University of the West of Scotland, believes the cost of living crisis has had an impact on festival attendances.
"We are living in a time of austerity and people, especially young people, are having to make decisions between, say, going to big gigs or the rest of their social life. No-one can pay for anything."
However Wallace, who performs as a musician herself and previously worked at DF Concerts when it was holding TRNSMT's famed predecessor T In The Park, also feels the Glasgow Green event struggled to establish a musical identity for itself.
"The programming of T In The Park was in line with the promoter's tastes, but also in alignment with young people's tastes, and T became this rite of passage for so many young people," she said.
"It was part of this Scottish identity and had this identity of its own, which I don't think TRNSMT ever really grasped. It just did not meet the cultural moment of the time."
TRNSMT launched in 2017, a year after the long-running T In The Park ended following a festival that saw the deaths of two teenagers and a host of organisational problems.
Unlike T, TRNSMT was based in a city and did not have camping, with Radiohead and Biffy Clyro among the early headliners.
McConnell told BBC Scotland News that if the festival doesn't go ahead it will be a blow to Scotland's music scene, as smaller stages there - like the BBC Introducing stage - can help emerging acts.
"There is a cultural loss that would come with this," he says.
"For better or worse, TRNSMT is Scotland's festival. Yes, we have Belladrum, Heartlands, Back Doune The Rabbit Hole and more independent festivals, but as the replacement for T in the Park, TRNSMT was the jewel in the crown of Scotland's festival scene.
"More importantly it is something for grass roots bands in Scotland to aspire to play. Local acts who were playing venues like McChuills in Glasgow last week are never going to be offered a slot at Summer Sessions.
"DF may be tight lipped about their plans - and the majority of music fans are hoping they actually have one - but until the public are told what's going on, they have no option but to assume that there are no plans."

Avukatı Şükrü Sarıdere, daha önceki açıklamalarında rapçinin doktorlar tarafından bilinçli olarak uyutulduğunu ve durumunun bir önceki haftaya göre çok daha iyi olduğunu söylemişti.

Oyuncu Aslıhan Malbora, sevgilisi Çağatay Ulusoy ile önümüzdeki ay yurt dışında nikah kıyacakları yönündeki haberleri yalanladı. İstanbul'da bir tiyatro oyunundan çıkarken gazetecilerin sorularını yanıtlayan Malbora, evlilik iddiası için "Hayır, öyle bir şey yok. Evlenmiyorum" dedi.
Çiftle ilgili son günlerde yalnız düğün değil, bebek iddiaları da gündeme gelmişti. Milliyet muhabiri Mesut Yılmaz'ın sorularını yanıtlayan Malbora'ya, hamilelik iddiaları nedeniyle yasal yola başvurmayı düşünüp düşünmediği soruldu. Oyuncu bu soruya "Hamile değilim, dava açmayı da düşünmüyorum" karşılığını verdi.
Malbora, son dönemde belirgin biçimde kilo veren Çağatay Ulusoy'un zayıflama iğnesi kullandığı yönündeki haberlere de değindi. Sevgilisinin iğne kullanmadığını söyleyen oyuncu, "Hayır, olmadı. Çok disiplinli bir diyet yapıyor" dedi.
Ulusoy da 19 Kasım akşamı Etiler'de Malbora ile birlikte görüntülendiğinde kilo verme sürecine ilişkin soruya "Diyet yaptım" yanıtını vermiş, yeni işinin başladığını ve sabah erken saatlerde sete gideceğini söylemişti.
Aslıhan Malbora, Show TV'de yayımlanan Üç Kuruş dizisinde canlandırdığı Leyla Çaka karakteriyle tanınıyor. Oyuncu, Her Yerde Sen ve Yaban Çiçekleri gibi dizilerde de rol aldı. Malbora ile Medcezir dizisiyle ün kazanan Ulusoy, Netflix dizisi Kübra'da birlikte oynadı; ikilinin ilişkisi Aralık 2024'te basına yansımıştı.
Çiftin önümüzdeki ay yurt dışında evleneceği iddiası son günlerde magazin gündemine taşınmıştı. Malbora'nın tiyatro çıkışındaki sözleri, hem evlilik hem de hamilelik söylentilerine verilen ilk doğrudan yanıt oldu.

Milyonlarca öğrencinin 9 günlük ilk molası yarın sona eriyor. 23 Kasım Pazartesi günü yeniden çalacak ders zili öncesinde öğrenci ve velilerin gündeminde tek bir soru var: İkinci ara tatil ne zaman yapılacak? MEB 2027 tatil takvimini açıkladı.
Okullarda birinci dönem ara tatili için son saatlere girildi. Hafta sonunun ardından pazartesi sabahı sınıflarına dönecek olan milyonlarca öğrenci ve öğretmen , birinci dönemin kalan maratonuna kaldığı yerden devam edecek. Ailelerin ve öğrencilerin gözü şimdiden eğitim yılının ikinci ara tatiline çevrildi.
Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı tarafından eğitim yılı başında ilan edilen resmi takvime göre, 2026-2027 döneminin ikinci ara tatili Mart ayında uygulanacak. Öğrenciler, 8 Mart 2027 Pazartesi günü ikinci kez ara tatile çıkacak. Beş iş gününü kapsayan bu dinlenme süreci, 12 Mart 2027 Cuma günü sona erecek.
Öncesindeki ve sonrasındaki hafta sonlarıyla birleştiğinde öğrenciler yine kesintisiz 9 günlük bir tatil fırsatı yakalayacak. Okullarda ders zili 15 Mart 2027 Pazartesi sabahı yeniden çalacak.
İlk ara tatilin tamamlanmasıyla birlikte birinci dönem, yarıyıl tatiline kadar kesintisiz sürecek. Yarıyıl tatilinin ardından başlayacak ikinci dönemde ise Mart ayındaki bu 9 günlük mola öğrencilere nefes aldıracak. Maratonun son düzlüğünde ise 2026-2027 eğitim -öğretim yılı, 25 Haziran 2027 Cuma günü karnelerin dağıtılmasıyla resmen tamamlanacak.
